key_insight: Instruct-Particulate turns 3D object articulation into a feed-forward prediction task guided by kinematic instructions, making it easier to reconstruct how object parts should move. The key breakthrough is that it combines mesh geometry with structured part/joint specifications to improve articulated 3D understanding with less reliance on dense labeled data.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of reconstructing articulated 3D objects when training data with detailed part and joint annotations is scarce. Existing methods often struggle to generalize to new object shapes and articulation layouts.
method: Takes a 3D mesh as input along with a target kinematic specification, including part descriptions, connectivity, joint types, and optional point prompts.
Uses a feed-forward model to predict articulated 3D structure directly from these instructions rather than relying on exhaustive per-object optimization.
Scales articulated object reconstruction by leveraging structured control signals to guide part segmentation and joint reasoning.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it offers a more scalable way to model articulated objects for animation, robotics simulation, and digital content creation. It also suggests a practical route to better generalization in 3D understanding when annotated data is limited.
